scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states” (preprints/Polynomial-PEPS-approximation-of-gapped-square-grid-ground-states-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 265 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0b55ba0b87ad0468), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an integer q ≥ 2 and constants J, ∆ > 0. There are constants C, c > 0, depending only on q, J, ∆, with the following property. For every L ≥ 2, consider any Hermitian Hamiltonian H = ∑︂ v∈ΛL hv + ∑︂ e∈E(ΛL) he, ∥hv∥, ∥he∥ ≤ J, (1.1) where each summand is supported on its designated site or edge. Suppose that H has a unique normalized ground vector Ω, up to phase, with ground energy E0, and H − E0I ≥ ∆ (︁ I − |Ω⟩⟨Ω| )︁ . (1.2) Then there is a nonzero PEPS Φ on the same grid with maximum bond dimension at most CLc such that min θ∈R ⃦ ⃦ ⃦ ⃦ Φ ∥Φ∥ − eiθ Ω ⃦ ⃦ ⃦ ⃦ ≤ L−1 . (1.3)
